newsitem.title: USA: Apple unveils speedy new Power Macintosh desktop PC.
newsitem.headline: Apple unveils speedy new Power Macintosh desktop PC.

text.p: Apple Computer Inc. Friday unveiled the Power Macintosh 6500 personal computer, a speedy machine featuring faster chips, improved multimedia capabilities, more memory and disk space.
The 6500, with prices starting at $2,000 up to $3,000, is aimed at students and small business owners, the company said.

The fastest model in the line features the 300-megahertz PowerPC chip, one of the fastest microchips on the market. One version of the machine also features electronics that capture video from the TV and let the user edit it, the company said.
The Power Mac 6500 is one of several new machines Apple plans to introduce this year to get its sales going again.

Last month, the company began selling an advanced laptop computer, which has been selling briskly, according to market researchers. Several more computers models, including one that will sell for less than $1,000, will be unveiled in coming months, the Cupertino, Calif., company has said.
The 6500 line replaces the Performa, a brand that was dropped last month as part of Apple's restructuring plan to cut one-third of its workforce and discontinue slow-selling products.
